newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK CB CHIEF SEEKS END TO PUBLIC CREDIT LINK.
newsitem.headline: TURK CB CHIEF SEEKS END TO PUBLIC CREDIT LINK.

text.p: Turkey's central bank governor Gazi Ercel said in a speech on Tuesday that ending the credit link between the bank and the public sector would boost confidence in the country's fight against inflation.

Speaking at the bank's annual shareholders' meeting, Ercel said a gradual lowering of the limit of short-term advances to the Treasury would help restrict the rise in the central bank's domestic loans.

The central bank's cash advances to the Treasury are limited at six percent of the difference between the expenditures in the current year's and the previous year's budgets, down from 10 percent in 1996. This limit will go down to three percent in 1998, according to the related law.
"The continued lowering of this limit in the coming years will further ease the application of the central bank's monetary policies," Ercel said in a speech to the meeting.
"My wish is that this item be completely discontinued in the near future as at other modern central banks," he said.

Ercel said uncertainty increased in the markets in 1996 as a result of political instability, entry into a customs union with the European Union and the failure to establish a political will in the struggle against inflation.
Annual wholesale price inflation stood at 77.0 percent in March, down from 84.9 percent in 1996.
In such an environment, the targets of monetary policy were directed towards maintaining and protecting stability in financial markets rather than lowering inflation, he said.
He said the central bank continued to monitor foreign exchange rates throughout 1996 with the aim of maintaining stability.
The level of Turkish interest rates was determined by the Treasury's domestic borrowing strategy and the central bank did not play a role in setting the level of interest rates, he said.

Turkish central bank's 1996 profits before tax surged to 85.36 trillion lira from 1.44 trillion the previous year. The transfer of a 33.33 trillion lira dividend to the Treasury was approved at the shareholders' meeting.
But Ercel said the dividend would be used to offset the bank's cash advances to the Treasury which stood at 383.3 trillion lira last week, compared to this year's limit of 505 trillion lira.
